rules.statement: A person who has obtained possession of land in a subordinate character, such as tenant or mortgagee, must show that by an overt act known to the person under whom he possesses, he has got rid of his subordinate status and assumed the character of a purchaser for prescription to commence.
rules.supporting_quote: Where a person who has obtained possession of the land of another in a subordinate character, e.g. as tenant or mortgagee, seeks to utilize that possession as the foundation of a title by prescription, he must show that by an overt act, known to the person under whom he possesses, he has got rid for this proposition, it will be found in such cases as Maduanwala v. the property ut dominus.

meta.parties: The Government Agent, Western Province v. Frederick Perera
